correctness.rationale: Invariance gives \(E[y]=bE[x]\) and hence \(aE|x|+(1-b)E[x]=1\). Decomposing into positive and negative parts yields the fixed-point simplex exactly. If one sign is absent, support invariance confines every complete orbit to one affine branch. Under \(0<b<1\) and \(a>1-b\), each branch matrix has one eigenvalue strictly inside and one strictly outside the unit circle, so its only bounded bi-infinite orbit is its fixed point. This proves endpoint rigidity and two-sided sign recurrence for every other invariant measure. The marginal pushforward law follows directly from \(y'=bx\). The packaged exact checker verifies all coefficient and classical-parameter arithmetic.

value.rationale: The left/right sign itinerary is the central symbolic coordinate in the established Lozi theory, while the classical literature proves existence of nontrivial physical invariant measures in the strange-attractor regime. The accepted theorem gives that coding a quantitative stationary law: positive and negative branch amplitudes lie on a fixed one-dimensional simplex whose vertices are exactly the two fixed points. The same affine-branch geometry proves a sharp rigidity statement that no non-fixed compact stationary state can live in only one symbolic half-plane. At the classical parameters this becomes the exact calibration \(11E[x_+]+6E[x_-]=5\), providing a simple invariant-measure consistency check for simulations or sampled physical measures and a structural bridge between symbolic coding and stationary amplitudes.
